'''Burton Wendroff''' (born March 10, 1930) is an American applied mathematician known for his contributions to the development of numerical methods for the solution of [[hyperbolic partial differential equation]]s. The [[Lax–Wendroff method]] for the solution of hyperbolic PDE is named for Wendroff (as well as for [[Peter Lax]]).

Wendroff is an adjunct professor at the Department of Mathematics and Statistics, [[University of New Mexico]]. He is also a retired fellow and associate at the [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]].

Wendroff is a primary author of the chess program Lachex. Together with co-author Tony Warnock, Lachex competed at two [[World Computer Chess Championships]] at Cologne (1986) and Madrid (1992).<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.grappa.univ-lille3.fr/icga/program.php?id=227|title=Lachex|publisher=univ-lille3.fr|access-date=20 March 2010|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20101009095705/http://www.grappa.univ-lille3.fr/icga/program.php?id=227|archive-date=9 October 2010|url-status=dead}}</ref><ref>{{cite journal|last=Wendroff|first=Burton|author2=Tony Warnock |author3=Lewis Stiller |author4=Dean Mayer |author5=Ralph Brickner |date=May 1993|title=Bits and pieces: constructing chess endgame databases on parallel and vector architectures|journal=Applied Numerical Mathematics|volume=12|issue=1–3|pages=285–295|doi=10.1016/0168-9274(93)90123-9|url=https://zenodo.org/record/1258409}}</ref>

==Career and research==
Wendroff received his B.A. degree in mathematics and physics from the [[New York University]] in 1951 and M.S. degree in mathematics from the [[Massachusetts Institute of Technology]] in 1952. After his M.S., Burt joined [[Los Alamos National Laboratory]] as a staff member. While at Los Alamos, he went to New York University to do his Ph.D. and received the degree under the supervision of [[Peter Lax]] in 1958.<ref>{{cite web|url=http://history.siam.org/pdfs2/Lax_final.pdf|title=An interview with Peter D. Lax|publisher=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]]|access-date=21 March 2010}}{{dead link|date=July 2017 |bot=InternetArchiveBot |fix-attempted=yes }}</ref> The title of his Ph.D. thesis was "Finite Difference Approximations to the Solutions of Partial Differential Equations". During 1966 to 1973, he served as a professor at the [[University of Denver]].<ref>{{cite web|url=http://www.math.unm.edu/~bbw/vita.08.ps|title=Resume: Burton Wendroff|access-date=21 March 2010|url-status=dead|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20100619015208/http://math.unm.edu/~bbw/vita.08.ps|archive-date=19 June 2010}}</ref>

His primary area of research involves the development of [[Numerical method|numerical schemes]] for [[hyperbolic partial differential equation]]s using [[finite difference method]]. Together with Peter Lax, he has developed the now classical [[Lax–Wendroff method]].<ref>{{cite book|last=LeVeque|first=Randall J.|authorlink=Randall J. LeVeque|title=Finite volume methods for hyperbolic problems|publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]]|year=2002|url=https://books.google.com/books?id=RbydDezW_KgC&q=classical+lax-wendroff+method&pg=PA146|isbn=9780521009249}}</ref><ref>{{cite book|last=Gustafson|first=Karl E.|author-link=Karl Edwin Gustafson|title=Introduction to partial differential equations and Hilbert space methods|publisher=[[Dover Publications]]|year=1999|edition=3|url=https://archive.org/details/introductiontopa00gust|url-access=registration|page=[https://archive.org/details/introductiontopa00gust/page/416 416]|quote=classical lax-wendroff method.|isbn=9780486612713}}</ref> He has developed two-dimensional HLLE [[Riemann solver]] and associated [[Godunov's scheme|Godunov-type difference scheme]] for [[gas dynamics]] problems. Wendroff has also made contribution to the early development of convergence study of [[finite element method]].<ref>{{cite web|last=Oden|first=J. Tinsley|authorlink=J. Tinsley Oden|url=http://history.siam.org/pdf/jtoden.pdf|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20220804133814/http://history.siam.org/pdf/jtoden.pdf|url-status=dead|archive-date=August 4, 2022|title=Historical Comments on Finite Elements|publisher=SIAM|access-date=21 March 2010}}</ref>

==Awards and honors==
Wendroff was elected as SIAM Fellow of [[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics]] for his "contributions to the numerical solution of [[partial differential equation]]s".<ref>{{cite web|url=http://fellows.siam.org/index.php?sort=year&value=2009|title=SIAM Fellows: Class of 2009|publisher=[[Society for Industrial and Applied Mathematics|SIAM]]|access-date=2010-03-21}}</ref>
